summary: HTTP/2 stream reordering at embeddings endpoint causes partial rerank responses and top-k misordering
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (ClaritySearch, enterprise) reports intermittent partial rerank responses and out-of-order top-k when using the embeddings+rerank flow over persistent HTTP/2 connections. Problem started after a proxy config change on 2026-02-28 that enabled HTTP/2 stream multiplexing at the edge for higher concurrency.

Impact:
- ~2-5% of requests to /v1/embeddings -> /v1/rerank pipeline return truncated rerank payloads (missing some items) or deliver items in inconsistent top-k order.
- Customer sees production search quality regressions and increased retries. Business impact: reduced search relevance, reported by QA and end customers.
- Affects only US-East prod region and customers using long-lived HTTP/2 connections with pipelined requests.

Environment:
- prod | us-east (edge proxy cluster ep-09)
- Redwood API v1 routed through HTTP/2-enabled proxy
- Customer client: Go net/http client with HTTP/2 enabled and a single persistent connection; batching at client layer.

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1. Establish a persistent HTTP/2 connection to api.redwood.ai (client keeps connection open).
2. Send an embeddings request for a batch of 64 inputs.
3. Immediately chain a rerank request using the embedding ids returned by the previous response (client reuses same connection stream).
4. Repeat at high rate (50-100 RPS) keeping the connection alive.
5. After ~10-100s of sustained usage, inspect rerank responses — some responses are partial (fewer items than requested) or items appear in wrong score order.

Expected behavior:
- Embeddings and rerank responses are complete, stable, and top-k ordering matches scores deterministically.

Actual behavior observed:
- Partial rerank payloads (missing items) and non-monotonic ordering of returned top-k items.
- Traces show embeddings response completed but downstream rerank receives a re-ordered or truncated body in ~2-5% of traces.

Logs / traces / telemetry (samples):
- Edge proxy (ep-09) logs: multiple HTTP/2 stream reset (RST_STREAM) and stream frame reorder warnings around 2026-02-28T18:12:xxZ.
- Reproducer trace id: trace-20260301-88fa3c (attached span logs show stream multiplexing on same connection and interleaved frames).
- Reranker service logs: request_id=rid-11c4b7; received body length 3612 bytes (expected 4872).
- Embeddings service: request_id=rid-11c4b7; upstream completed with full embedding payload.
- No consistent 5xx from runtime; errors manifest as data corruption/partial reads.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Disable HTTP/2 keepalive/pipelining on client (force new connections per request) which eliminates the issue for their workload. Customer was able to fall back to short-lived HTTPS connections as stopgap.

Notes on scope and frequency:
- Only reproduced in envs where edge proxy multiplexing is enabled and client reuses the same HTTP/2 connection heavily.
- Not observed for HTTP/1.1 clients.

Attachments:
- Selected proxy logs (ep-09) and application traces (trace-20260301-88fa3c).
- Minimal repro harness (Go client) included in linked PR for internal testing.

Next steps recommended:
1) (Immediate) Apply mitigation at edge: disable HTTP/2 stream multiplexing for affected edge pool for enterprise customers until root cause is fixed. Deployed by SRE on 2026-03-02 as a hotfix.
2) (Investigation) Instrument proxy frame sequencing metrics and add assertion checks in streaming-proxy to detect out-of-order frames or premature stream closures.
3) (Fix) Harden parsing logic in streaming-proxy to ensure per-stream frame ordering and validate payload completeness before forwarding to reranker.
4) (Backport) Add guard in embeddings-service and reranker to verify content-length vs received bytes and reject/trigger telemetry on mismatch.
5) (Customer comms) Draft incident note and recommended client config for long-lived connections.

Expected ETA for full fix: 2-3 sprints after investigation (tentative).
investigation_notes:
03/01: Reproduced locally using Go client with HTTP/2 on. Observed re-ordered frames in proxy pcap dump.
03/02: SRE applied mitigation to disable multiplexing for ep-09 and reported immediate drop in incidents for ClaritySearch.
Hypothesis: recent proxy change enabling concurrent stream prioritization introduced a race where frames for different streams are forwarded out of per-stream order under high concurrency. Streaming-proxy uses an older HTTP/2 implementation that lacked strict per-stream serialization under load.
Action items: capture pcap on multiple edge nodes, add CI test for stream-order preservation, and open PR to upgrade HTTP/2 library or add serialization layer.
Related PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4271 (contains repro harness and initial fix to sequencing buffer).
comments:
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-01: Customer reported intermittent missing rerank items and top-k order issues. Provided initial triage and requested traces.
Miguel Santos (SRE) 2026-03-01: Collected pcap and proxy logs; saw RST_STREAM + frame reorder warnings. Tentatively blocking on edge config.
ClaritySearch (Customer) 2026-03-01: Confirmed issue goes away when HTTP/2 disabled client-side.
Miguel Santos (SRE) 2026-03-02: Hotfix applied to edge pool ep-09 to disable multiplexing for affected customers; monitoring.
Elena Korhonen (Backend) 2026-03-03: Began code changes to sequencing buffer in streaming-proxy, added unit tests for order-preservation. Linked PR for review.
Aisha Patel (Support) 2026-03-03: Notified customer of hotfix and temporary workaround; scheduled weekly cadence with ClaritySearch until full fix is deployed.
resolution: Mitigation deployed (disabled HTTP/2 multiplexing on affected edge pool). Root-cause fix in progress (sequencing buffer hardening and HTTP/2 lib upgrade). Customer reverted client-side workaround after hotfix; monitoring continues. Follow-up: backport to other edge pools and add CI tests for stream ordering.
